connector: You have read The Whipping Boy and two weeks of true articles. Now be a history detective. Which parts of the stories match real life long ago, and which parts did storytellers change? And why would they change them?

vcloze1.h1: Find the word for a person who studies the past.
vcloze1.why: A historian studies old records to learn about the past.

vcloze2.h1: Find the word that means true to the facts.
vcloze2.why: Accurate means correct and true to the facts.

vcloze3.h1: Find the word for making something seem more perfect than it was.
vcloze3.why: To idealize is to make something seem better than it really was.

vcloze4.h1: Find the word for facts that support a claim.
vcloze4.why: Evidence is the facts that support a claim.

cards.title: Job Spotlight: The Scribe
cards.sub: A real job in the Middle Ages
cards.todo: Read about this real job. Then read the two questions and the article.
text: A scribe was a person whose job was writing. The root scribe means write!
Before there were printing presses, scribes copied every book by hand, letter by letter.
Scribes also wrote down laws, letters and records. Much of what historians know about the Middle Ages comes from what scribes wrote.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. Today you get to be a history detective. Stories borrow from real life, and then they change things. Let’s find out what is real.
transcripts.guide1: Word study review. Roll script and scribe words, find the sentence that wandered off, and pick endings.
transcripts.guide2: Read the last article. Sort what is real from what stories made up.

notes.wordParts: The root script or scribe means write. describe = to write about something. manuscript = written by hand. One root, two spellings.
notes.grammar: A paragraph has one main idea, often in the first sentence (the topic sentence). The other sentences are details that support it. A sentence that does not support it is off the topic.
notes.spelling: -ful means full of (hopeful). -less means without (hopeless). -ness turns a describing word into a thing (kindness). -ly tells how something was done (quickly).
notes.wgrd: Stories borrow from history but add imagination. Ask what is real, what was changed, and why a storyteller changed it.
vocab: a person who studies and writes about history using evidence
to make something seem better or more perfect than it really is
facts used to support a claim

plate.alt: A painting of a queen in a white gown tapping the shoulder of a kneeling knight in red with a sword, while people watch
plate.credit: The Accolade · Edmund Blair Leighton, 1901 · private collection · Public domain
plate.look: This painting is not from the Middle Ages. Edmund Blair Leighton painted it in 1901, about 600 years after the time it shows. A queen taps a kneeling knight on the shoulder with a sword to make him a knight. Everything looks clean and perfect. This is how storytellers imagined knights: the ideal, not a record of real life.
plate.lookBtn: Tap to learn about this painting of a knight

virtue.name: diligence
virtue.title: Diligence Watch: Is someone working hard?

items.t: Apprentices really did spend years learning a trade.
items.why: Learning a trade for years takes diligence.

items.t: In real medieval life, most peasants never met a king.
items.why: That is about who met a king, not about someone working.

items.t: Whipping boys may or may not have existed.
items.why: That is something historians argue about, not someone working hard.
